entries.title: Psalms 139:1
segments: In this remarkable psalm the divine omniscience and omnipresence are set forth with wonderful vividness and power; not, however, as abstract truths, but with particular reference to the psalmist's own case.  The all seeing God, who formed him in the womb, has watched over and shaped his course every moment,
.  He knows his servant's uprightness of heart, and will distinguish between him and the wicked,
.  He knows his servant's weaknesses and failings also; David therefore prays that God will reveal them to him, and lead him in the way everlasting,

entries.title: Psalms 139:2
segments: Afar off; to God's omniscience there is no limit of distance or time.

entries.title: Psalms 139:3
segments: Compassest; or, winnowest; narrowly examinest, as one examines wheat by sifting it.

entries.title: Psalms 139:4
segments: With God concealment and hypocrisy can have no place.  All within us and around us is "naked and opened unto the eyes of Him with whom we have to do."

entries.title: Psalms 139:9
segments:
If I take the wings of the morning; fly westward on the beams of the morning sun. 
 
  The uttermost parts of the sea; the most remote regions of the west, the same as "the islands of the sea."
From the position of the Mediterranean, the Hebrews were accustomed to speak of the west as the sea.  Thus in
, where the four cardinal points are enumerated, the last mentioned is seaward, that is, westward.

entries.title: Psalms 139:10
segments: God's power over us is as absolute as his knowledge of us.  His omnipotence and omniscience alike compass us about, so that there is no escape from either.

entries.title: Psalms 139:13
segments: Hast possessed my reins; hast them in thy knowledge and control, as their Maker.

entries.title: Psalms 139:14
segments:
Fearfully and wonderfully; in a manner adapted to excite astonishment and awe. 
 
Our bodies are such a wonderful exhibition of God's incomprehensible skill, power, and goodness, as should inspire us with the deepest feelings of admiration and awe.

entries.title: Psalms 139:15
segments:
My substance; my frame. 
 
  Curiously wrought; literally, embroidered; a description of the delicate and complicated tissue of the human body. 
 
  In the lowest parts of the earth; hid from view, as if in the depths of the earth; the same as "in secret," and "in my mother's womb."

entries.title: Psalms 139:16
segments:
Yet being unperfect; before my birth. 
 
  Written; as an architect has before him a written description and plan of the house which he is building. 
 
  Which in continuance were fashioned; were fashioned by a continuous growth that went on day after day.

entries.title: Psalms 139:17
segments: Meditation on God's wonderful dealings with themselves and others, is one of the sweet and blessed employments of the righteous.

entries.title: Psalms 139:18
segments: I am still with thee; I am with thee, in thy care, and in my meditations.

entries.title: Psalms 139:22
segments: God hates the character and ways of the wicked, and the feelings of all righteous men are in harmony with his.

entries.title: Psalms 139:24
segments: The way everlasting; the old way appointed by God from ancient times; the same as "the old paths, where is the good way."

Wicked men love self-delusion, and willingly remain ignorant of themselves.  But the good man earnestly desires and prays that God would search his heart, show him all his hidden faults, and help him to repent of them and forsake them.
